page: Amazon Web Services m8g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong memory capabilities, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier. Memory bandwidth tests show strong results for large block read-only operations at 296.67 GB/sec and write operations at 133.88 GB/sec. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, fall within the average range. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression shows strong performance at 200.91 GB/sec, while database operations score strongly on Passmark. LLM inference speeds are average for text generation on medium models but weak for prompt processing.

Given its ARM-based architecture and dedicated core allocation, the m8g.4xlarge offers a resource-dense profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be handled externally. This instance is suited for workloads such as database operations, web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose application hosting.
